title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
abstract: arXiv:2611.09454v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Agent skills are short documents that teach a language model how to handle a class of tasks. To save context, these documents are increasingly compiled into low-rank adapters (LoRA), which keep the behaviour but lose the text: an adapter is hard to read, edit, audit or move to another model. We ask whether the skill document can be written back from the adapter and its frozen base model, and we score each recovered document by the share of the original's key instructions it states and by the tasks it solves. Reading the weights alone recovered little with the methods we tried; a learned map from weights to text passed on about one bit of the document. Running the adapter worked much better. The Executing Writer, a small writer trained on top of the adapted model, recovers 39-44% of the key instructions of held-out skills, against 1.3-1.5% with another skill's adapter, and on adapters fitted to 41 external skills its documents restore 8

translated_title: 从LoRA到语言：从适配器中恢复技能文档
translated_abstract: 智能体技能是教会语言模型如何处理一类任务的简短文档。为了节省上下文，这些文档越来越多地被编译成低秩适配器，后者保留了行为却丢失了文本：适配器难以阅读、编辑、审计或迁移到其他模型。我们探究能否从适配器及其冻结的基础模型中“写回”技能文档，并根据恢复出的文档陈述了原文档关键指令的比例以及它所解决的任务来为每个恢复文档评分。在仅读取权重的各种尝试方法下，恢复效果甚微；一个从权重到文本的学习映射只能传递文档约一比特的信息。而直接运行适配器的效果要好得多。Executing Writer（执行写手）是一个在适配后模型之上训练的小型写手，对留出技能它能恢复39-44%的关键指令，而使用另一个技能的适配器仅有1.3-1.5%；在拟合到41个外部技能的适配器上，其文档恢复了8……（原文摘要在此截断）
tldr: 提出Executing Writer方法，通过在适配后模型之上运行并训练一个小型写手，可从LoRA适配器及其冻结基座模型中恢复约39-44%的技能文档关键指令，而仅靠读取权重几乎无法恢复任何内容。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Executing Writer, a small writer trained on top of the adapted model that recovers 39-44% of a skill document's key instructions from its LoRA adapter by running it, whereas reading the weights alone recovers almost nothing.
